title: Exchange and projection transformations
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$, and put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $S$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible, let $X,Y,Y'$ be finite-type $S$-schemes, and let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ be separated finite-type $S$-morphisms [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Form the Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
 X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
 f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
 Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y.
\end{array}
$$

**Finite coefficients.** Work first with $\Lambda=A$ in the ambient unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], for the schemes $T$ occurring below, using the sites and derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and the tensor product of [def-weil-derived-tensor]. The pullbacks, direct images, and adjunctions $Lu^*\dashv Ru_*$ are those of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], agreeing with the finite operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-direct-image]; write $\eta_u$ and $\varepsilon_u$ for their units and counits. For constant coefficients $Lu^*=u^{-1}$. Throughout the finite-level formulas let $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $L\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be arbitrary. Let
$$
\theta:Lf'^*Lg^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg'^*Lf^*
$$
be the composite of the pullback-composition isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] and $gf'=fg'$. Define the direct-image exchange transformation to be the ambient ringed exchange of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange], namely
$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Ex}_{*,K}:Lg^*Rf_*K
&\xrightarrow{\eta_{f'}}Rf'_*Lf'^*Lg^*Rf_*K\\
&\xrightarrow{Rf'_*(\theta_{Rf_*K})}Rf'_*Lg'^*Lf^*Rf_*K
\xrightarrow{Rf'_*Lg'^*(\varepsilon_{f,K})}Rf'_*Lg'^*K.
\end{aligned}
$$
Equivalently, this is the mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] whose transpose under $Lf'^*\dashv Rf'_*$ is $Lg'^*(\varepsilon_{f,K})\circ\theta_{Rf_*K}$.

**Chosen compactification.** Choose a compactification $c=(j,p)$, $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$, with $p j=f$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $\overline X'=\overline X\times_Y Y'$, with $p':\overline X'\to Y'$ and $\bar g':\overline X'\to\overline X$, and let $j':X'\hookrightarrow\overline X'$ be the base change of $j$. Extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero] is applied termwise using its exactness [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Write
$$
 Rf_!^c=Rp_*j_!,\qquad Rf'_!^{c'}=Rp'_*j'_!,\qquad c'=(j',p').
$$
These formulas define the compactification-relative composite functors on the ambient finite-coefficient categories; in the field-base setting they are the candidates of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Let
$$
 \beta_K:L\bar g'^*j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!Lg'^*K
$$
be the canonical pro-etale open-immersion base-change isomorphism [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change], applied to the upper open-immersion square. Define
$$
 \operatorname{Ex}_!^c(K):Lg^*Rf_!^cK
 \xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}_{*,p}(j_!K)}Rp'_*L\bar g'^*j_!K
 \xrightarrow{Rp'_*(\beta_K)}Rp'_*j'_!Lg'^*K
 =Rf'_!^{c'}Lg'^*K.
$$

**Projection transformation.** All finite-level tensor products are the derived sheaf tensor products [def-weil-derived-tensor]. For a morphism $u:V\to W$ and $F,G\in D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, let $\mu_{u;F,G}:Lu^*(F\otimes_A^L G)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lu^*F\otimes_A^L Lu^*G$ be the ambient derived tensor-pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. For $M\in D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $N\in D(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, define the typed map
$$
a_{u,M,N}:Lu^*(Ru_*M\otimes_A^L N)\xrightarrow{\mu_{u;Ru_*M,N}}Lu^*Ru_*M\otimes_A^L Lu^*N\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{u,M}\otimes1}M\otimes_A^L Lu^*N,\qquad
\pi_{u;M,N}=Ru_*(a_{u,M,N})\circ\eta_{u,Ru_*M\otimes_A^L N}.
$$
Thus $\pi_{u;M,N}:Ru_*M\otimes_A^L N\to Ru_*(M\otimes_A^L Lu^*N)$ is the counit-defined natural projection map of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Let
$$
 \gamma_{K,L}:j_!K\otimes_A^L Lp^*L
 \xrightarrow{\sim}j_!(K\otimes_A^L Lj^*Lp^*L)
 \xrightarrow{\sim}j_!(K\otimes_A^L Lf^*L)
$$
be the open-immersion projection isomorphism [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula] followed by $Lj^*Lp^*\cong Lf^*$. Define
$$
 \operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}^c:
 Rf_!^cK\otimes_A^L L
 \xrightarrow{\pi_{p;j_!K,L}}Rp_*(j_!K\otimes_A^L Lp^*L)
 \xrightarrow{Rp_*(\gamma_{K,L})}Rf_!^c(K\otimes_A^L Lf^*L).
$$
In particular this applies to $K\in D^b_c(X,A)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. The maps are composites of the specified natural transformations; no assertion of invertibility of $\operatorname{Ex}_*$, $\operatorname{Ex}_!^c$, or $\operatorname{PF}^c$ is included.

**Other coefficient stages and domains.** For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, the same formulas define transformations relative to the following supplied data: categories and operation functors of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-direct-image, def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], on full domains closed under all the displayed composites; adjunctions $Lu^*\dashv Ru_*$ on those domains; natural pullback-composition and tensor-pullback isomorphisms of the displayed types; and natural open-immersion isomorphisms $\beta$ and $\gamma$ of the displayed types. Supply also the identifications of the chosen-compactification functors with $Rp_*j_!$ on these domains. At the integral stage, for every integer $m\geq1$ supply finite-reduction identifications with the operations at $A_{E,m}$, compatible with the transition maps $A_{E,m+1}\to A_{E,m}$, carrying the units, counits and comparisons to their finite-level counterparts. At the rational stage, these maps are the rationalizations of integral maps. For algebraically closed coefficients, choose an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and an embedding of $E$ into it; the maps are represented over a common finite coefficient field, with supplied scalar-extension comparisons intertwining the units, counits and comparisons. Require these scalar-extension comparisons to be identities for identity field extensions and to satisfy the composition cocycle for towers of finite coefficient fields, using the transition functors and composition identifications of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Thus the component over a common finite field is taken as its morphism class in the displayed common-stage category; further scalar extension gives the same class. There is no reduction functor from rational coefficients to $A_{E,n}$. Here integral pullback and tensor mean completed derived pullback and completed tensor, and the integral categories are [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]; rational and algebraically closed categories are [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. With these supplied data replace $A$ by $\Lambda$ in the three composites above, for $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ in their domains. This is a definition from the supplied operation and comparison data, not an assertion that those data exist on all bounded constructible categories over an arbitrary $S$.

The superscript $c$ records a choice. On the etale-origin field-base domain, [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] compares the underlying functors. Dropping $c$ from the transformations additionally requires that those comparisons intertwine the displayed composites. That compatibility, and the existence and preservation assertions needed for higher coefficients, are separate theorems, not defining properties or consequences asserted here.

statement_change.old_statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq1}$, and put $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $S$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is
invertible, let $X,Y$ be finite-type
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] $S$-schemes, and let every morphism
below be an $S$-morphism. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, where
the finite-level coefficient category is the finite-torsion constructible
category [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]; the latter coefficient
categories are obtained by derived completion, rationalization, and the
common-stage construction. Use the derived pullback, tensor, and
internal-Hom operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the derived
direct image [def-weil-derived-direct-image], and the compact-support direct
image [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. The finite-Tor and
interval conditions are the finite-Tor
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] and constructible-interval
[def-weil-constructible-intervals] conditions. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated
and of finite type, let $Y'$ be a finite-type $S$-scheme and let $g:Y'\to Y$
be separated and of finite type, and set $X'=X\times_Y Y'$, with projections
$g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$. Consider the resulting Cartesian square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
 X' & \xrightarrow{g'} & X\\
 f'\downarrow && \downarrow f\\
 Y' & \xrightarrow{g} & Y
\end{array}
$$

The direct-image exchange transformation

$$
 \operatorname{Ex}_*:\;Lg^*Rf_*\longrightarrow Rf'_*Lg'^*
$$

is adjoint to the composite

$$
 Lf'^*Lg^*Rf_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg'^*Lf^*Rf_*
 \longrightarrow Lg'^*,
$$

whose second arrow is the counit of $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$. If $f=\bar f\circ j$
is a compactification [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], the
compact-support exchange map

$$
 \operatorname{Ex}_!:\;Lg^*Rf_!\longrightarrow Rf'_!Lg'^*
$$

is represented by $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ for $\bar f$, followed by the
canonical identification $L\bar g'^*j_!\cong j'_!Lg'^*$, where $\bar f':\bar
X'\to Y'$ and $\bar g':\bar X'\to\bar X$ are the base changes of $\bar f$,
and $j':X'\hookrightarrow\bar X'$ is the base change of $j$; the independence
of this map from the compactification is the compactification-coherence
proposition.

For $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, the projection
transformation is

$$
 \operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}:Rf_!K\otimes^L L
 \longrightarrow Rf_!(K\otimes^L Lf^*L).
$$

For this compactification it is the direct-image projection transformation
for $\bar f$, followed by $j_!K\otimes^LL\bar f^*L\cong j_!(K\otimes^LLf^*L)$.
These are natural transformations with the displayed sources and targets.
statement_change.what: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: the imported arbitrary-base statement does not specify domains for higher-coefficient composites and attributes exchange-map independence to a proposition comparing only functors. For S the infinite disjoint union of Spec(k) and f the disjoint union of P^r_k -> Spec(k), f is proper of finite type over S, but the constant finite sheaf has nonzero R^(2r)f_* at the r-th point, so Rf_* is not globally bounded. Use the ambient unbounded categories at finite coefficients and supplied operation/adjunction/comparison data at other stages, as the ambient-typing and typed-exchange units intend. Retain chosen compactifications until an intertwining theorem is available. Also type the tensor-pullback comparison on two target-site objects and distinguish integral finite reduction from rationalization and common-field scalar extension. Second reading: all finite-level objects are explicitly quantified; integral reduction data range over every positive level and respect tower transitions; scalar-extension comparisons obey identity and composition coherence so the common-field formula defines a morphism class.
